description: Revenue-by-segment earnings deck for a diversified industrial conglomerate, in the style of a segment-reporting supplement.
provenance: Modeled on the segment-detail slides that diversified industrials (GE/Honeywell/Emerson style) attach to quarterly earnings packages: consolidated view, per-segment revenue and margin detail, mix chart, and segment-versus-segment commentary. Deliberately exercises a four-series clustered bar chart across four quarters (16 bars), a pie chart with five slices, a comparison slide, and KPI cards carrying explicit card styles.

content.title: Segment margin walk vs Q2 2025
content.subtitle: Operating margin by segment, year-over-year
bulletPoints: Automation & Controls: 24.8% vs 23.6% — price/cost positive for the seventh straight quarter; software mix now 18% of segment revenue
Aerospace Systems: 22.1% vs 20.4% — commercial aftermarket up 19%; supply-chain premiums easing on castings and fasteners
Energy Solutions: 17.9% vs 18.3% — margin down 40 bps on LNG project timing; backlog margin remains accretive
Building Technologies: 15.2% vs 14.1% — restructuring savings of $22M realized; China property exposure now under 6% of segment sales
Corporate & eliminations: $(48)M vs $(51)M — lower incentive-compensation accrual
Total segment operating margin: 21.3% vs 20.4% (+90 bps)

content.title: Orders and backlog
content.subtitle: Demand indicators by segment
bulletPoints: Total backlog of $12.4B, up 11% YoY; approximately 62% expected to convert within twelve months
Automation & Controls orders up 9% organically; discrete automation recovering off a low base in semiconductors
Aerospace Systems book-to-bill of 1.18x, including a $410M widebody environmental-control-systems award
Energy Solutions orders down 3% on timing of two Middle East LNG packages; funnel up 14% sequentially
Building Technologies orders up 5%; data-center cooling orders more than doubled YoY and now exceed a $500M annual run-rate

content.title: "Three of our four segments expanded margins while growing organically — portfolio pruning and the 80/20 operating cadence are doing exactly what we said they would."
content.subtitle: Marcus Whitfield, Chairman & Chief Executive Officer
